citations.quote: Would you go back 10 or 20 years if you could?

cue.text: Would you go back 10 or 20 years if you could?

citations.quote: How much would I pay to return to my life 20 years ago, when I was 26? Or even 10 years ago, when I was 36? Honestly? Nothing.

response.text: The author values their current life and wouldn't pay to return to their past self 10 or 20 years ago.

citations.quote: Jimmy Carr shared this thought on The Diary of a CEO, and it genuinely stayed with me.

situation.text: The author reflects on a thought shared by Jimmy Carr about valuing one's current life stage.

citations.quote: How much would I pay to return to my life 20 years ago, when I was 26? Or even 10 years ago, when I was 36?
But gratitude is not about pretending that everything is perfect. Sometimes it is simply recognising that the life you may miss one day is already happening right now.

observation.text: The text compares one's current life with the past to encourage reflection and gratitude.

citations.quote: In 20 years, you would give everything to be where you are right now. At this age, in this body, living this exact life.
You might miss your current age, your health, your body, the people around you and even the problems that now feel so important.
